warmup.text: In Chapter 20, Isaac finally reaches Naomi, and the chapter takes a hard turn. Your reading lens this week is figurative language. Watch for comparisons, where one thing is described as another. Each time, ask what the picture makes you feel.

words.text: Two roots this week mean light. One came from Latin, one from Greek. Then long words about books, built from parts you already know. In the lantern game, build each word from its parts, and watch the lantern light up.

reading.text: Read Chapter 20 in your book. Watch what Naomi does to stay strong, and what goes wrong with Isaac's plan. This chapter is hard. Take it slowly. Then do the Read Like a Writer box and the Virtue Watch.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 20. Then a new piece of writing begins: a paragraph about the novel. Today you only plan. Choose a topic, write your claim, and find two pieces of evidence.

do: Read the three lenses.
Tap the one you will use today.
Keep it in mind as you read. You will use it at the end.
how.why: A comparison can make you feel something the author never says.
how.use: You will use this when you answer the chapter questions.

do: Read the two roots and what they mean.
Tap a word, then tap its meaning.
Match all four.
how.why: This week's chapters are full of moonlight, firelight and glowing ghosts. These roots name light.

how.why: These words show up in this week's chapters. Knowing them first keeps the reading smooth.

Think through the questions.
Tap Now check your thinking.

how.why: A pronoun should point back to only one noun.

Think through the questions.
Tap a word, then tap its column.
how.why: Long book words are short parts stacked together.

do: Read Chapter 20 first.
Answer each question in 2 or more sentences.
Use details from the chapter as evidence.
how.why: These questions check what happened and what the author shows you.

do: Choose one topic from the list.
Write your claim in one sentence.
Find two pieces of evidence in the book and note them.
how.why: A literary analysis makes a claim about a book and proves it with evidence.
how.use: Tomorrow you will draft the paragraph.

do: Read what perseverance means.
Read the example from this week.
After you read, sort the moments at the end of this tab.
Read the chapter introduction below.
Open your book and read Chapter 20.
Then do the Read Like a Writer box and the Virtue Watch below.

glossary.meaning: words that describe one thing as if it were another, not meant word for word
showing how two different things are alike

miss.autograph: Find g-r-a-p-h at the end: auto + graph. Graph means write.
miss.chronicle: Find c-h-r-o-n at the start. Chron means time.
miss.anachronism: Find c-h-r-o-n in the middle: ana + chron + ism. Chron means time.
miss.dialogue: Find l-o-g-u-e at the end: dia + logue. Log means word or speech.
miss.monologue: Find l-o-g-u-e at the end: mono + logue. Log means word or speech.
miss.paragraph: Find g-r-a-p-h at the end: para + graph. Graph means write.
miss.photograph: Look at the end, not the start: photo + graph. Graph means write.
miss.prologue: Find l-o-g-u-e at the end: pro + logue. Log means word or speech.

game.title: Light the Lanterns
game.sub: This week's word game · 4 words today
game.look: Each lantern on the branch waits for one word. Read the meaning, then tap the word parts in order to build the word. When the word is whole, its lantern lights up.

Tap the first part of the word.

Tap Next lantern.

game.doneLine: Come back tomorrow to light more.

words.why: photo (light) + copy. A copier uses a flash of light.

words.means: a person who takes pictures with a camera
words.why: photo + graph + er: a person who writes with light.

words.means: the light that is shone on something
a part at the end of a book, after the story is over
words.why: epi (after) + logue (words): the words after the story.

art.title: Moonlight, Tarpon Springs
art.alt: A painting of a dark grove of trees at night, with the moon low in the sky, a small fire and a woman walking.
art.look: George Inness painted this moonlit night in Tarpon Springs, Florida, in 1892. It is not Isaac's road, but it feels like the start of Chapter 20: a quiet camp at night, a small fire, and the moon over the trees.
art.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting
art.creator: George Inness

virtue.name: perseverance
virtue.title: Perseverance or not?
virtue.intro: You just read Chapter 20. Read each moment. Tap Perseverance or Not perseverance.

items.t: Leader shouts, “Who were you talking to?” Naomi keeps saying, “No one.”
items.why: She keeps protecting Isaac and Nita, even when Leader gets louder. That is perseverance.

items.t: Isaac tries to drag Naomi away, but his hands pass right through her.
items.why: That is something he cannot do. What he does next is what counts.

items.t: Isaac tells Nita, “We will not leave her here,” and hurries to find Joseph.
items.why: The plan went wrong, and he does not give up. He goes for help.

items.t: The other soldiers stand and stare without saying a word.
items.why: They do nothing. Perseverance means you keep working toward what is right.
